UNIVERSITY GRANTS COMMISSION (UGC)
NOTIFICATION
New Delhi, the 12th May, 2026

No. F. 1-1/2026(UGC/ABC) — In exercise of the powers conferred by clauses (f) and (g) of sub-section (1) of Section 26 of the University Grants Commission Act, 1956, and in alignment with the National Education Policy (NEP), the UGC hereby notifies the establishment of the Academic Bank of Credits (ABC) in Higher Education Regulations.

1. Short Title and Commencement:
These regulations shall be called the University Grants Commission (Establishment and Operationalization of Academic Bank of Credits in Higher Education) Regulations, 2026. They shall come into force with immediate effect.

2. Objectives of the Academic Bank of Credits:
To facilitate student mobility across higher education institutions (HEIs) through a formal system of credit accumulation, credit transfer, and credit redemption. ABC is a digital/virtual depository that holds academic credits earned by students from registered HEIs, allowing students to seamlessly exit and re-enter academic programs.

3. Key Provisions & Operational Framework:
(a) Mandatory Registration: All Central, State, Deemed-to-be, and Private Universities accredited by NAAC with an 'A' grade or above must register with the Academic Bank of Credits portal within six months.
(b) Credit Deposit: Registered HEIs shall upload student course credits digitally to the ABC ledger under the student's unique ABC ID.
(c) Credit Validity: Credits deposited in the ABC shall have a maximum shelf life of seven (7) academic years. After seven years, the credits will expire and cannot be redeemed for any academic award.
(d) Credit Redemption: For awarding degrees, diplomas, or certificates, the credit redemption process shall be initiated by the awarding HEI through the ABC database.
(e) Multiple Entry and Exit: Students can exit at the end of Year 1 with an Undergraduate Certificate, Year 2 with an Undergraduate Diploma, Year 3 with a Bachelor's Degree, or Year 4 with a Bachelor's Degree with Research, provided they accumulate the minimum required credits:
   - Certificate: 40 Credits (after Year 1)
   - Diploma: 80 Credits (after Year 2)
   - Degree: 120 Credits (after Year 3)
   - Honours/Research: 160 Credits (after Year 4)

4. Institutional Compliance and Infrastructure:
Every registered HEI shall establish an ABC Cell headed by a Nodal Officer. The cell is responsible for mapping academic curricula to national credit frameworks, verifying student transcripts, uploading credit data, and resolving credit validation issues. HEIs must upgrade their IT systems to interface with the national ABC API.

5. Penalties for Non-Compliance:
HEIs failing to register on the ABC platform or upload student credit logs within the stipulated period shall be liable to penalties, including:
(a) Suspension of UGC development grants.
(b) De-recognition of the institution's capacity to admit new students in specific programs.
(c) Warning letters and negative grading during NAAC reaccreditation.

MINISTRY OF EDUCATION
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA
NATIONAL RESEARCH FOUNDATION (NRF)
GUIDELINES FOR SEED FUNDING AND COLLABORATIVE GRANTS

Date: 3rd April, 2026

Subject: Guidelines for the Allocation and Administration of Research Grants under the National Research Foundation (NRF) for Universities and Colleges.

The Government of India is pleased to announce the operational rules for research funding distributed through the National Research Foundation (NRF). The goal is to seed, grow, and facilitate research in India's universities, colleges, and research institutions.

1. Eligibility and Categorization:
Research funding will be distributed across three tiers:
(a) Category A (Seed Grants): Up to INR 20 Lakhs for early-career faculty members (within 5 years of PhD appointment) to establish laboratory infrastructure and baseline studies.
(b) Category B (Collaborative Research): Up to INR 1.5 Crores for joint projects involving at least two HEIs, with mandatory involvement of one State Public University or College.
(c) Category C (Industry-Academia Partnerships): Up to INR 3 Crores for projects co-sponsored by private sector companies, with industry contribution of at least 30% of the total budget.

2. Intellectual Property (IP) and Publishing:
(a) Open Access Mandate: All research papers resulting from NRF-funded projects must be published in open-access journals. Authors must deposit their preprint and accepted manuscripts in the National Digital Library repository.
(b) IP Ownership: Intellectual property developed under NRF grants shall reside jointly with the primary institution and the researchers. For Category C, IP licensing rights will be shared with the industry sponsor under fair-use agreements.
(c) Commercialization Sharing: Net royalties generated from commercialization must be distributed as: 50% to the researchers, 30% to the institution, and 20% back to the NRF revolving research fund.

3. Monitoring, Documentation, and Timelines:
(a) Semester Reviews: Principal Investigators (PIs) must submit bi-annual progress reports and digital utilization certificates (UCs) via the NRF portal.
(b) Funding Release: Funds will be released in three annual installments. The second and third installments are strictly conditional on the PI utilizing at least 75% of the previously allocated funds and submitting satisfactory progress logs.
(c) Zero-Tolerance for Plagiarism: Any instance of academic dishonesty, plagiarism exceeding 10% similarity index, or data fabrication shall lead to the immediate termination of the grant, blacklisting of the PI for 10 years, and recovery of the entire funded amount as government land revenue.

4. Administrative Workload for HEIs:
Each participating college and university must setup a central Office of Dean (Research & Development). This office will be audited annually by NRF compliance officers. Institutions must maintain transparent financial books, hire project research fellows strictly through national level entrance tests, and manage the procurement of equipment through the government e-Marketplace (GeM) portal.

analysis.document_title: UGC Academic Bank of Credits (ABC) Implementation Guidelines
layman_summary: Establishes a unified national digital credit vault called the Academic Bank of Credits (ABC).
Integrates student credit tracking directly with Digilocker systems for automatic validation.
Mandates all universities and colleges to register and upload semester transcripts within 30 days of results.
Enables flexible Multiple Entry and Exit options: Certificate (40 credits), Diploma (80 credits), and Degree (120 credits).
Establishes strict shelf-life limits: all accumulated credits strictly expire after seven (7) academic years.
Requires each HEI to establish a local 'ABC Cell' headed by a Nodal Officer to manage mapping schemas.
Failing to onboard will result in severe penalties including NAAC score cuts and suspension of UGC development grants.

positives: Complete student mobility allowing credit transfer across different colleges.
No financial or degree penalty for temporary study drops or exit cycles.
Direct online credit status logs through verified Digilocker APIs.
negatives: Credits automatically expire and disappear strictly after 7 academic years.
Added responsibility to trace credit balances before lateral entry.
opportunities: Opportunity to earn specialized multi-disciplinary joint degrees.
Flexible part-time course credit accumulation options.

positives: Standardized grading mapping frameworks across state-level colleges.
Increased educational modularity allowing creative elective course designs.
negatives: Heavy administrative coursework grading mapping tasks.
Mandatory alignment of syllabi with rigid national NHEQF credit parameters.
opportunities: Opportunity to launch high-demand online certificate modules.
Specialized academic credit mentorship and nodal leadership roles.

positives: Standardized national course credit integration and digital transcript indexing.
Ability to attract a massive volume of returning lateral-entry students.
negatives: Excessive tech infrastructure setup cost for affiliated colleges.
Strict 30-day post-exam credit upload timelines.
Catastrophic penalties including suspension of developmental grants.
opportunities: Flexible partnerships with state and central universities.
Corporate skill-based joint program launches.

positives: 100% digital, transparent, paperless academic records audit path.
Standardized ranking metrics for international credit equivalents.

analysis.document_title: UGC Promotion of Equity in Higher Education Institutions Regulations, 2026
layman_summary: Mandates the strict prevention of discrimination against SC, ST, OBC, Minorities, Women, and Differently-abled students in all HEIs.
Requires every university and college to establish a dedicated 'Equal Opportunity Cell' (EOC) within 60 days.
Mandates the appointment of a senior professor as the 'Anti-Discrimination Officer' (ADO) to head local grievance boards.
Enforces strict timelines: all discrimination complaints must be investigated and resolved within fifteen (15) working days.
Prohibits any form of harassment, hate speech, or segregated seating/dining in academic and residential blocks.
Requires HEIs to publish a transparent student charter outlining safety pathways and anti-discrimination rights.
Failing to implement these measures will result in severe penalties, including stripping of university status and suspension of research development funds.
